_README: Bidirectional file-size budget ledger for scripts/check-file-size.mjs. path -> one-line reason. Every entry MUST still be over its dialect hard cap; when a file drops to/under the cap its exclusion goes STALE and --strict fails, forcing you to delete the entry so the budget re-arms. Do not add a file here to dodge a split — add it only with a real reason and a plan.
streamhost/scripts/streamhost-station.sh: 651L; shfmt reformat pushed it just over the 600 hard cap; split candidate
streamhost/stations/irix/x11-runtime.sh: 781L; tile launcher (boot + 2 watchdogs + instant-restore #44 + audio fifo + mamectl socket plane #45); cohesive lifecycle unit, split candidate
scripts/build-guests/tiles/os2warp.sh: 620L golden builder, just over the 600 hard cap; split candidate
spa/src/three/useStreamControl.ts: 602L, just over hard cap; trim or fold into the streamClient split (#13)
scripts/build-guests/tiles/win95.sh: golden builder (1065L); long install script, split candidate
scripts/build-guests/tiles/armeval.sh: 736L golden builder; carries the merged ARM Evaluation System bake-off — the blue-ink identity gate, the ARM-BASIC white-ink gate, the 30-frame red-nag sweep, the stopped-screendump reset check and the five-action keyboard proof, plus the header recording why -rom3 / -fdc acorn1770 / ui.ini skip_warnings cannot be simplified; split candidate (the ink gates belong in a shared bridge-gates.sh)
streamhost/streamhost/src/mame_sock.rs: mamectl socket sink (~840L incl. temporary SH_MAMESOCK_TRACE campaign instrumentation); drops back under the cap when the trace knob is removed
scripts/build-guests/tiles/pdp11.sh: 784L golden builder; embeds the forkpty console driver that answers SIMH's ':' bootstrap prompt and single-user ^D (SIMH's own EXPECT/SEND does not fire against 2.11BSD's boot block), plus the AIO-deadlock and throttle assertions; split candidate
scripts/build-guests/tiles/c128.sh: 630L golden builder, just over the 600 hard cap; carries the -80col VDC selection, the deferred CP/M disk attach (with -8 the KERNAL autoboots CP/M and BASIC never shows) and the GO64 freeze re-measurement; split candidate
spa/src/ui/keyboard/keyboardProfiles.ts: 682L; the on-screen-keyboard profile registry, pushed over the 600 hard cap by the Sinclair/Dragon/KC-85 wave (zxspectrum, zx81, dragon, kc854, sinclairql each add a profile). Genuine split candidate: the row builders and the Family/OS_FAMILY tables are one concern and the per-machine PROFILES literal is another, so PROFILES should move to its own module
scripts/build-guests/tiles/bbcmicro.sh: 624L golden builder for a DISABLED candidate whose build wave was interrupted before the golden bake; it will be revisited when the tile is finished, and should be split then
spa/src/scene/machines.ts: 606L; the parametric MODELS table and the ASSEMBLIES_BY_TILE map in one file, pushed over the 600 hard cap by the Xerox/Iris wave (daybreak and indyr4400 each add an assembly plus its justification comment). Genuine split candidate, and the split also removes a recurring merge hazard: every new tile appends to ASSEMBLIES_BY_TILE at the same spot, so two parallel tile branches conflict there every time (they did on this merge). ASSEMBLIES_BY_TILE should move to its own module. Deferred only because a tile branch was mid-flight in this file; do it as soon as the Xerox wave lands.
scripts/dev/migrate-tile.sh: 624L, the bookworm->trixie per-tile driver. It sat at 583L (97% of the cap) and three waves spent the remaining headroom on correctness fixes it could not run without: launch/poll/stop moved into scripts/lib/box-detached-build.sh after a quiet 20s poll interval was read as `builder exited <line-count>` and rolled healthy builds back on top of LIVE tiles (decos, plus4, bbcmicro -- three separate incidents), a rollback that now fails CLOSED rather than touching an overlay under a surviving builder, and staging streamhost/stations/<tile> for the builders that read host-side sidecars from there. The seam is clean and already visible: the file is a nine-step driver plus SIX box-side programs it ships as quoted heredocs (the preflight PROBE python, and the stop / backup / bake / restart / rollback shell blocks, ~230L together). Those move to scripts/dev/migrate-tile.d/ as real files that shellcheck can see on their own -- today they are strings, so the gate never lints them, which is the second and better reason to do it. That leaves the driver as argument parsing, the step sequence and the epilogue, ~410L, and deletes this entry. Deferred only because waves 3,5,6,7 run this script unchanged and a split mid-migration is the wrong risk; do it once the ledger is all-trixie.
